```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
    collapse = TRUE,
    comment = "#>"
)

has_runtime_pkgs <-
    requireNamespace("tempdisagg", quietly = TRUE) &&
        requireNamespace("zoo", quietly = TRUE)
```

This vignette shows the `tsflow` CSV workflow end to end:

- define a pipeline in CSV
- inspect it with `plan_pipeline()`
- inspect the dependency DAG
- execute it with injected `ts` inputs

## Example Pipeline

The package installs a small example mapping as CSV together with a sidecar
metadata file. `tsflow` reads the CSV, merges the sibling metadata, and
compiles the result into the same structured pipeline model used by the YAML
format.

```{r}
example_path <- system.file("examples", "gdp_construction.csv", package = "tsflow")
cat(paste(readLines(example_path), collapse = "\n"))
```

```{r}
meta_path <- system.file("examples", "gdp_construction.meta.yml", package = "tsflow")
cat(paste(readLines(meta_path), collapse = "\n"))
```

## Define Transforms

This example uses real R functions with the same calling style that `tsflow`
expects at execution time. They ship next to the CSV as
`gdp_construction_transforms.R`:

```{r}
transforms_path <- system.file("examples", "gdp_construction_transforms.R", package = "tsflow")
```

```{r, eval = has_runtime_pkgs, code = readLines(transforms_path)}
```

Collect them in a named list to pass to `tsflow`:

```{r, eval = has_runtime_pkgs}
library(tsflow)

transforms <- list(jsa = jsa, real_gr_nom = real_gr_nom, a2q_sum = a2q_sum)
```

## Plan The Pipeline

Plan the pipeline before running it:

```{r, eval = has_runtime_pkgs}
plan <- plan_pipeline(
    path = example_path,
    transforms = transforms
)

plan
plan$dag$order
dag_edges(plan$dag, include_labels = TRUE)
```

If `igraph` and `visNetwork` are installed, you can inspect the DAG
interactively in the HTML vignette:

```{r, eval = has_runtime_pkgs && requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("visNetwork", quietly = TRUE)}
dag_to_visnetwork(plan, upstream_of = "construction.deflator.quarterly")
```

## Execute The Pipeline

Raw inputs are injected as named `ts` objects. The vignette uses a small
packaged dataset for this step:

```{r, eval = has_runtime_pkgs}
data("gdp_construction_inputs", package = "tsflow")
inputs <- gdp_construction_inputs

result <- execute_pipeline(
    path = example_path,
    inputs = inputs,
    transforms = transforms
)
```

`result$values` contains the full executed state. Because the example CSV does
not define explicit outputs, `result$outputs` defaults to the derived series:

```{r, eval = has_runtime_pkgs}
names(result$outputs)
result$outputs$gdp.nominal.quarterly
result$outputs$construction.real.quarterly
result$outputs$construction.deflator.quarterly
```

You can also recover the executed DAG and the full upstream calculation path for
any result node:

```{r, eval = has_runtime_pkgs}
result$dag
result_path(result, "construction.deflator.quarterly")
result_subgraph(result, "construction.deflator.quarterly")
```

```{r, eval = has_runtime_pkgs && requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("visNetwork", quietly = TRUE)}
subgraph <- result_subgraph(result, "construction.real.quarterly")
dag_to_visnetwork(result, nodes = subgraph$nodes)
```

You can also execute only the subgraph needed for one target:

```{r, eval = has_runtime_pkgs}
constr_nom_result <- execute_pipeline(
    path = example_path,
    inputs = inputs,
    outputs = "construction.nominal.quarterly",
    transforms = transforms
)

constr_nom_result$plan$order
names(constr_nom_result$values)
constr_nom_result$outputs$construction.nominal.quarterly
```

To run steps in parallel, or to keep results between sessions, use
`tar_tsflow()` with `targets`; see the README section "Running With targets".

## Document The Pipeline

`series_lineage()` describes one series: its definition step by step, which
input feeds which transform argument, the shared parameters it uses, its raw
sources and the series that use it. Passing a result adds its status, period
and latest value:

```{r, eval = has_runtime_pkgs}
descriptions <- c(
    jsa = "Temporal disaggregation onto the seasonally adjusted indicator",
    real_gr_nom = "Real level from growth rates and a base-year level",
    a2q_sum = "Annual to quarterly, Chow-Lin with an indicator"
)

lineage <- series_lineage(
    plan,
    "construction.real.quarterly",
    transform_descriptions = descriptions,
    result = result
)
```

Printing it gives the Markdown page, rendered here:

```{r, eval = has_runtime_pkgs, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("::: {.lineage-output}\n")
print(lineage, heading_level = 3, links = FALSE)
cat("\n:::\n")
```

`document_pipeline()` writes the same information for every series as Markdown
pages plus an index, ready for GitHub, pkgdown or Quarto:

```{r, eval = has_runtime_pkgs}
docs_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "gdp-lineage")
files <- document_pipeline(plan, docs_dir, transform_descriptions = descriptions, result = result)
basename(files)
```
